image_description: A large whale breaches the ocean surface, displaying a dark dorsal side with mottled white patches and a lighter ventral side. A prominent, elongated pectoral fin is visible on the left side of the body. The head is angled upward, revealing the throat area. In the background, a small boat with people is visible on the horizon.

The snout area looks slightly blunt and lacks clear definition of specific grey whale cranial features.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin clearly shows the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white speckling consistent with barnacles and cyamids (whale lice).

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed; baleen plates are internal and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A large pectoral fin is clearly visible, but it is exceptionally long and slender (reaching ~1/3 body length), which contradicts the Grey Whale checkpoint describing 'broad and paddle-shaped' flippers. This morphology is diagnostic of a Humpback Whale, not a Grey Whale.
